bib.title: ReClor: A Reading Comprehension Dataset Requiring Logical Reasoning

read.skipped: Appendix C example tables 17-26 and Appendix E figure axes skimmed only (example questions, plot labels)

question: Can a reading-comprehension dataset of exam logical-reasoning questions, split into biased (EASY) and non-biased (HARD) test items, show whether pre-trained models really reason?
hypothesis: Models exploit answer-option biases to score well without reasoning, so a debiased HARD split will expose weak logical reasoning.
contributions: ReClor, a RC dataset requiring logical reasoning, with EASY/HARD test split from option-only baselines
Evaluation of state-of-the-art models showing good EASY, near-chance HARD performance

method.summary: 6,138 GMAT/LSAT logical-reasoning questions with 4 options. Option-only baselines (5 models x 4 seeds) define EASY test items; the rest are HARD. Ten baseline models are fine-tuned on ReClor (optionally after RACE) and compared with 10 graduate students.

datasets.name: ReClor
datasets.split: 4,638 train / 500 val / 1,000 test; EASY 440 of test (rest is HARD)
datasets.source: GMAT and LSAT exams and practice exams (91.22% actual exams); five options reduced to four by deleting one random wrong option and shuffling; non-commercial research only
datasets.preprocessing: shuffle option order, randomly delete one wrong option

training.objective: multiple-choice scoring: final hidden vector of aggregate token to fully connected layer(s), score per option
training.lr_schedule: Linear decay (transformers); Bi-LSTM decay 0.5 every 10 epochs
training.seeds: 4 seeds per model for the option-only EASY/HARD identification; seed count for Table 7 not stated

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: percent of test questions answered correctly; reported overall, EASY, HARD

eval.protocol: Humans: 100 random test questions split into ten tests, one per student, averaged. Ceiling set at 100%. No significance tests.

evidence.quote: We use a batch size of 24 and ﬁne-tune for 10 epochs.

results.claim: Fine-tuned pre-trained models score about 75% on the EASY (biased) set but only about 30% on the HARD set.
results.setup: ReClor test (1,000; EASY 440 / HARD 560), BERT/XLNet/RoBERTa/GPT/GPT-2 fine-tuned on ReClor only, input (C,Q,A)
results.note: HARD ~30% from 'perform poorly on HARD set with only around 30% accuracy' in same paragraph
results.quote: these models only perform well on EASY set with around 75% accuracy, showing these models have an outstanding ability to capture the biases of the dataset, but they perform poorly on HARD set with only around 30% accuracy

results.claim: RoBERTa-large fine-tuned on RACE then ReClor reaches 65.1% test accuracy, above graduate students (63.0%).
results.setup: ReClor test, RoBERTa-large, RACE then ReClor, input (C,Q,A)
results.table: Table 7, row RoBERTaLARGE (C,Q,A) with RACE check, column Test

results.claim: The same model scores 54.3% on HARD after RACE fine-tuning (40.0% without), against 57.1% for graduate students.
results.table: Table 7, row RoBERTaLARGE (C,Q,A) with RACE check, column Test-H

results.claim: Graduate students (10 students, 100 sampled test questions) score 63.0 overall, 57.1 on EASY and 67.2 on HARD.
results.setup: 100 random test samples split into ten tests, one per student, averaged
results.note: Authors say EASY/HARD gap may be due to few students
results.table: Table 7, row Graduate Students, column Test

results.claim: XLNet-large without RACE: 56.0 test, 75.7 EASY, 40.5 HARD.
results.setup: ReClor HARD test, XLNet-large, (C,Q,A), no RACE

results.claim: Option-only input (A) is already well above chance: RoBERTa-large 43.2 test, 69.5 on EASY but 22.5 on HARD.
results.setup: ReClor test, answer options only, RoBERTa-large

results.claim: Adding the question to the options gives little gain; adding context gives a large gain.
results.quote: Further adding context causes signiﬁcant boost, showing the high informativeness of the context.

results.claim: EASY set is the union of data points four-seed-consistently solved by option-only models: 440 of 1,000 test items.
results.setup: Five base models (GPT, GPT-2, BERT-base, XLNet-base, RoBERTa-base), 4 seeds each, options only
results.quote: Finally, we get 440 data points from the testing set CTEST

results.claim: Chance of passing four seeds by guessing is 0.39%.
ReClor has 6,138 questions split 4,638 train / 500 val / 1,000 test.

results.quote: They are divided into training set, val-idation set and testing set with 4,638, 500 and 1,000 data points respectively.

results.claim: Right options are slightly longer than wrong ones (23.06 vs 21.82 average length).

results.quote: On HARD set, the three models perform poorly on certain types such as STRENGTHEN, WEAKEN and ROLE which require extensive logical reasoning.
